stack.summary: Parcel Locker is a synthetic Java service that uses only the Java standard library. The 35-file prepared snapshot contains Java domain, application, adapter, configuration, CLI, and test sources plus Markdown, properties, and SQL; 29 files have full parsed structural coverage and six are file-level records, with TimeSource.java partial because of an unsupported construct and five non-Java files unsupported. README.md documents a javac-only baseline with no Maven or network dependency.

sections.heading: Runtime and dependencies
sections.content: Source imports use java.time, java.util, java.nio.file, java.io, and java.util.Properties alongside the fixture packages. No dependency manifest or third-party library is present in the prepared file set; runtime dependency claims are limited to the standard library.

sections.heading: Coverage
sections.content: Prepared coverage is 35/35 included files, with 197 symbols, 109 imports, and 145 relationships. Six records are file-level only: README.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md, config/default.properties, sql/schema.sql, AGENTS.md, and the partially parsed TimeSource.java interface.

architecture.summary: The implementation separates domain state and policies from application orchestration, ports, adapters, configuration, and CLI composition. DeliveryApplicationService coordinates repository lookups, ZoneAwareLockerPolicy selection, Delivery and Parcel transitions, persistence, and notifications; Main wires those ports to in-memory adapters and a fixed clock.

sections.heading: Application flow
sections.content: accept constructs a Parcel, asks the assignment policy to choose from available lockers in the requested zone, assigns a deadline, saves delivery and locker state, then emits deliveryReady. collect and cancel delegate lifecycle checks to Delivery and Parcel while releasing the associated locker.

sections.heading: Ports and adapters
sections.content: DeliveryRepository, LockerRepository, NotificationPort, ManifestReader, and TimeSource define application-facing boundaries. InMemoryDeliveryRepository, InMemoryLockerRepository, ConsoleNotificationAdapter, CsvManifestReader, and FixedTimeSource provide executable adapters in this fixture.

structure.summary: Source packages are organized under com.blueprint.fixture.lockers: domain contains Parcel, Delivery, Locker, statuses, and assignment policy; application contains use-case services, commands, receipts, and ports; adapter contains in-memory repositories, CSV input, notifications, and a fixed clock; config contains property loading; Main composes the executable sample. Three Java main-style tests cover application behavior, configuration/manifest translation, and CLI wiring.

sections.heading: Source tree
sections.content: The repository has src/, tests/, config/, docs/, and sql/ roots. The Java source set has no framework or generated-code layer; each package is small and directly referenced by the CLI or tests.

sections.heading: Domain vocabulary
sections.content: DeliveryStatus and ParcelStatus represent lifecycle values; LockerSize provides fit ordering; Delivery, Parcel, and Locker hold state with guarded transitions. Application records CreateDeliveryCommand, ManifestLine, and DeliveryReceipt carry boundary data.

conventions.summary: The Java code uses final classes, records for boundary values, enums for statuses and sizes, constructor null checks, requireText validation for identifiers, Optional for absent locker and deadline values, and repository/port interfaces for application dependencies. IDs and zones are trimmed before storage where requireText is used; pickup codes are passed as strings and compared at collection.

sections.heading: Validation and state
sections.content: Parcel, Delivery, Locker, CreateDeliveryCommand, and ServiceConfig reject blank text and null required values. Delivery and Parcel guard legal transitions with DomainException; Locker guards ownership when assigning or releasing.

sections.heading: Selection ordering
sections.content: ZoneAwareLockerPolicy filters available lockers by zone and size fit, then chooses the minimum LockerSize and ID. The ordering is implemented with Comparator and is observed by the application test.

testing.summary: The checked-in tests are executable Java main classes using assertions and explicit checks rather than a visible test framework. DeliveryApplicationServiceTest covers smallest-fitting assignment, successful collection and release, wrong pickup-code rejection, and oversized rejection; ConfigurationAndManifestTest covers property parsing and CSV translation; MainSmokeTest exercises CLI composition with temporary files. README documents the javac and java invocation, but no production build or CI configuration is present in the prepared snapshot.

sections.heading: Behavior exercised
sections.content: The application test verifies notification order, receipt status and deadline, persistence state, locker occupancy/release, and rejection invariants. ConfigurationAndManifestTest verifies header and blank-row handling plus trimming and enum translation. MainSmokeTest verifies config and manifest arguments reach Main.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.content: These tests are fixture-level executable checks. They do not establish concurrency, remote persistence, carrier protocol compatibility, or production operational guarantees.

integrations.summary: Integration surfaces are local standard-library adapters. PropertiesServiceConfigLoader reads pickup.window.hours and default.zone; CsvManifestReader reads five-column CSV rows and ManifestImportService maps them to CreateDeliveryCommand values; Main composes these with in-memory repositories, a fixed clock, and console notifications. sql/schema.sql is an illustrative relational shape for a future adapter, while the executable baseline remains in memory.

sections.heading: CLI
sections.content: Main accepts an optional config path and optional manifest path. With a manifest it imports rows and prints a receipt count; without one it prints a readiness message for the configured default zone.

sections.heading: Persistence and notification
sections.content: In-memory repositories are the only executable persistence adapters. ConsoleNotificationAdapter reports ready and collected events; no network client, database driver, or durable store is shown.

concerns.summary: This is an intentionally bounded synthetic fixture. The executable composition uses process-local in-memory repositories, so assignments disappear when Main exits; sql/schema.sql describes a future relational adapter and is not wired. The prepared map has full structural coverage for 29 files and file-only coverage for six records, including a partial Java interface and five unsupported-language files, so claims about those files are limited to observed file content. No evidence establishes production-scale concurrency, durability, security hashing, or external protocol behavior.

sections.heading: Lifecycle and data handling
sections.content: Delivery keeps pickupCode in an in-memory String and compares it during collection; receipts and the console adapter use delivery and parcel identifiers/statuses rather than the code. cancel persists the cancelled delivery and releases its locker but does not call the notification port in the observed application method.

sections.heading: Unsupported or future surfaces
sections.content: README.md and docs/OPERATIONS.md are file-level evidence, as are properties and SQL files. The SQL schema includes a pickup_code_hash column, but no executable adapter or hashing implementation is present in the Java source.

capabilities.name: Accept and assign delivery
capabilities.summary: Create a delivery from a command, choose a fitting locker in the requested zone, set the pickup deadline, persist assignment state, notify readiness, and return a receipt.

capabilities.name: Collect delivery
capabilities.summary: Verify an assigned delivery's pickup code, mark delivery and parcel collected, release the locker, persist the state, and emit a collection notification.

capabilities.name: Cancel delivery
capabilities.summary: Cancel a queued or assigned delivery, release an assigned locker, mark its parcel returned, and save the delivery and locker state.

capabilities.name: Import CSV manifest
capabilities.summary: Read a five-column CSV manifest with optional header and blank-row handling, convert locker sizes and trimmed fields, and delegate each line to delivery acceptance.

capabilities.name: Zone-aware locker selection
capabilities.summary: Filter available lockers to the parcel zone and fitting sizes, then select the smallest fitting size with locker ID as the tie-breaker.

capabilities.name: CLI composition
capabilities.summary: Compose configuration, repositories, policy, clock, notifications, application service, and optional manifest import from command-line arguments.

capabilities.name: Properties configuration
capabilities.summary: Load a positive pickup window and nonblank default zone from a properties file into ServiceConfig.

capabilities.name: In-memory persistence adapters
capabilities.summary: Store deliveries and lockers in process-local maps behind DeliveryRepository and LockerRepository interfaces.

claims.statement: README describes Parcel Locker as a small invented Java service, bounded to standard-library APIs, with a javac-only executable baseline and no Maven or network access.

DeliveryApplicationService.accept rejects duplicate tracking IDs, constructs a Parcel, delegates locker selection, sets a clock-based pickup deadline, marks and assigns the delivery, saves both aggregates, emits deliveryReady, and returns a DeliveryReceipt.

ZoneAwareLockerPolicy filters available lockers by parcel zone and LockerSize fit, then chooses the minimum size and ID; the application test observes a medium parcel choosing N-11 over larger or out-of-zone alternatives.
collect requires an assigned Delivery and exact pickup code, then marks the parcel collected, releases its locker, saves delivery and locker state, and emits deliveryCollected.

cancel allows queued or assigned Delivery states, changes the delivery to CANCELLED, releases an assigned locker, marks the Parcel returned to depot, and saves the resulting state; the observed method does not notify.
CsvManifestReader skips empty lines and a case-insensitive trackingId header, requires five columns, trims fields, and converts the locker-size column with LockerSize.valueOf.
ManifestImportService maps each parsed ManifestLine to CreateDeliveryCommand and delegates it to DeliveryApplicationService.accept, returning the resulting receipt list.

Main loads configuration from an optional first argument, creates in-memory delivery and locker repositories, composes ZoneAwareLockerPolicy, ConsoleNotificationAdapter, FixedTimeSource, and DeliveryApplicationService, and optionally imports a second-argument manifest.
PropertiesServiceConfigLoader parses pickup.window.hours into a positive Duration and default.zone into ServiceConfig, while config/default.properties supplies 48 hours and NORTH defaults.
InMemoryDeliveryRepository and InMemoryLockerRepository implement the repository behavior with process-local maps, lookup/save operations, and available-in-zone locker queries.

README documents direct javac and java execution for three main-style test classes and Main; the checked-in tests exercise assignment and collection, rejection invariants, configuration and CSV translation, and CLI wiring.

Because Main composes only in-memory repositories and README says the executable fixture uses in-memory adapters, assignments are expected to be lost when the process exits; the source does not establish durable or concurrent persistence.

sql/schema.sql defines an illustrative locker and delivery relational shape, including pickup_code_hash and a locker foreign key, while README says the executable baseline deliberately uses in-memory adapters.
